catalog_quote: Stress in Amri Karbi is predictable. Therefore, we assume that there is no stress in the underlining form of a word. However, the surface form has stress. So, the following stress pattern for Amri Karbi can be proposed: Amri Karbi stress parse into binary-syllabic feet, i.e. each foot has two syllables, starting at the right-most edge of the word. Amri Karbi has both primary and secondary stress. Feet in Amri Karbi are right-headed, i.e. iambic. The primary stress resigns on the first foot at the foot head position and the secondary stress falls on the head of the second foot. Stress in Amri Karbi is not contrastive; however, it interacts with the surface realization of tone (see more in §2.4.3). ... audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The classification (predictable, non-contrastive final primary stress; right-to-left iambic feet; secondary on head of second foot; domain = phonological word; clitics and -po/-pe/-so unstressed) rests on the best and only reference grammar of the language (Philippova 2021, 468 pp incl. front matter), which we hold as the open-access Helsinki PDF; every quoted passage and locator (§2.4.1 pp.45-46 exx. 2.6-2.8, p.27, §3 pp.61-62, §2.4.3 p.51) was confirmed verbatim in the text we hold. The Glottolog bibliography offers nothing stronger: the one other item is an unpublished 2012 wordlist-based conference phonology that Philippova herself reviews and supersedes. The one open item found and downloaded today (Teronpi 2025, Ri-Bhoi variety, 8 pp) treats segments only and is explicitly silent on prosody, so it neither confirms nor challenges the record. no reclassification or re-read is indicated.
